our issues list is noisy with CVEs that don't affect osquery. This will
ignore those to help us focus on the dependencies we should update now.

This PR adds 25 ignored-cves entries to

## Summary

Adds `ignored-cves` entries to
`libraries/third_party_libraries_manifest.json` for **25 dependency
CVEs** that have been triaged as **not impacting osquery**. Each was
opened by the automated dependency-CVE checker; this records the
completed impact analysis so the checker stops re-filing them, without
waiting on a dependency bump.

Triage follows the reachability model in `ASSURANCE.md` (client-only
agent, never listens for inbound connections, statically linked, does
not shell out). For each CVE we confirmed the vulnerable code path is
either not compiled into osquery or not reachable through the way
osquery uses the library.

## CVEs added to the ignore list

| Library | CVE | Issue(s) | Why osquery is not affected |
|---|---|---|---|
| popt | CVE-2026-18839 | #9093 | popt is pulled in only transitively by
librpm/libcryptsetup (Linux); osquery's own CLI uses gflags. The
vulnerable CLI-argument/help-text paths are never exercised by the
library APIs osquery links. |
| popt | CVE-2026-18739 | #9092 | (same as above) |
| openssl | CVE-2026-75803 | #9091 | OpenSSL is used only as a
client-side TLS-over-TCP stack (Config/Logger/Enroll). None of these
land in a reachable path: no CMP, no QUIC, no CMS_decrypt, no one-shot
EVP_Cipher AEAD, and OCSP response checking is not enabled. Verified
across every vendored consumer (boost, aws-sdk-cpp, librdkafka, thrift,
librpm, yara). |
| openssl | CVE-2026-63076 | #9090 | (same as above) |
| openssl | CVE-2026-63075 | #9089 | (same as above) |
| openssl | CVE-2026-63074 | #9088 | (same as above) |
| openssl | CVE-2026-63073 | #9087 | (same as above) |
| openssl | CVE-2026-63072 | #9086 | (same as above) |
| openssl | CVE-2026-54876 | #9067 | (same as above) |
| openssl | CVE-2026-54874 | #9066 | (same as above) |
| openssl | CVE-2026-18798 | #9064 | (same as above) |
| openssl | CVE-2026-14457 | #9063 | (same as above) |
| openssl | CVE-2026-14456 | #9062 | (same as above) |
| sqlite | CVE-2025-71316 | #9083 | The affected feature (CLI shell, or
an optional module such as zipfile / FTS) is not compiled into osquery's
SQLite amalgamation and runtime extension loading is off. |
| sqlite | CVE-2026-11824 | #8936 | (same as above) |
| sqlite | CVE-2026-11822 | #8935 | (same as above) |
| sqlite | CVE-2025-70873 | #8908 #8834 | (same as above) |
| libarchive | CVE-2026-16517 | #9082 | CVE-2026-16517 is in the ZIP
writer, which osquery never invokes (its only writer path is PAX tar, no
encryption). CVE-2025-60753 is in the bsdtar CLI and osquery is already
on the fixed 3.8.1. |
| libarchive | CVE-2025-60753 | #8901 #8767 | (same as above) |
| util-linux | CVE-2026-13595 | #8988 | osquery compiles only libblkid
(superblock probing) for the block_devices/disk_encryption tables. The
vulnerable code lives in the mount(8)/other CLI tools, which are not
built, and the partition-probing chain is never enabled. |
| util-linux | CVE-2026-27456 | #8919 #8842 | (same as above) |
| lzma | CVE-2026-34743 | #8903 #8833 | The vulnerable sequence
(lzma_index_decoder followed by lzma_index_append on a crafted
zero-record index) requires manual lzma_index manipulation that osquery
never performs. |
| libdpkg | CVE-2025-6297 | #8902 #8663 #8765 | osquery compiles only
libdpkg (lib/dpkg, lib/compat); the vulnerable dpkg-deb
control-extraction code is not built. |
| librpm | CVE-2026-44605 | #9100 | Heap overflow in RPM's NDB backend
triggered by parsing a crafted NDB database file. osquery compiles the
NDB backend and reads RPM databases, but `rpm_packages` only ever opens
the default, root-owned system RPM DB (`rpmReadConfigFiles(nullptr,
nullptr)`); an unprivileged user cannot supply a crafted DB to the path
osquery reads. |
| boost | CVE-2016-9840 | #8584 | CVE-2016-9840 was fixed in zlib 1.2.9;
osquery vendors zlib 1.3.1 (PR #8625), so the fixed code is what is
linked. (Tracked here under boost due to the CPE.) |

> Note: the thrift, sleuthkit, and zlib CVEs originally included here
have been dropped — those dependencies were since upgraded on `master`

remediated by the bump rather than ignored.

## Summary

Adds `ignored-cves` entries to
`libraries/third_party_libraries_manifest.json` for **25 dependency
CVEs** that have been triaged as **not impacting osquery**. Each was
opened by the automated dependency-CVE checker; this records the
completed impact analysis so the checker stops re-filing them, without
waiting on a dependency bump.

Triage follows the reachability model in `ASSURANCE.md` (client-only
agent, never listens for inbound connections, statically linked, does

4.15.0 fixes two out-of-bounds reads that are reachable through
osquery's `device_file` / `device_hash` / `device_partitions` tables
(which open a device path and let TSK auto-detect the filesystem):

- CVE-2026-40025 — OOB read in the APFS keybag `wrapped_key_parser` (fix
`8b9c9e7d4`); tracked in #8829 / #8905.
- CVE-2026-40026 — OOB read + infinite loop in the ISO9660
`parse_susp()` parser (fix `a95b0ac21`); tracked in #8836 / #8906.

The version update also includes fixes for CVE-2026-40024 (`tsk_recover`
path traversal — a CLI tool osquery doesn't build, see #8828/#8904) and
additional NTFS bounds hardening.

What changed:

- Submodule `libraries/cmake/source/sleuthkit/src` → `01de0345`
(`sleuthkit-4.15.0`)
  - `libraries/third_party_libraries_manifest.json` → 4.15.0
- Version strings (`PACKAGE_STRING`/`PACKAGE_VERSION`/`VERSION`) bumped
to 4.15.0 in the four
`config/{macos,linux}/{aarch64,x86_64}/tsk/tsk_config.h` overlays
- `CMakeLists.txt`: four source files added. In 4.15.0 the core
`tsk/fs/fs_open.c` and `tsk/img/raw.c` unconditionally call new
encryption/logical-filesystem helpers, so these previously-unreferenced
files are now required to link:
    - `tsk/fs/encryptionHelper.cpp`, `tsk/fs/logical_fs.cpp`
    - `tsk/img/logical_img.c`, `tsk/util/file_system_utils.c`

— they're gated behind `HAVE_LIBMBEDTLS`, which osquery's `tsk_config.h`
does not define, so no new dependency (`mbedtls`) is introduced. For
osquery's raw block-device access, these new paths are effectively
no-ops.

Closes #8828 #8904 (tsk_recover) (not-affected and also handled by the
ignore-list PR)
